text:
sam: Heads up — after yesterday's int4 activation-scaling change on the batcher branch we started seeing a perf regression + some structured-output failures on the eval suite. Model: rwd-gpt-13b-quant-int4. p95 latency +35% and intermittent JSON schema parse errors. Also spike in hallucination score on the structured eval set.

kiran: Do we have a run id / deploy that introduced this? Can you paste the repro steps or logs? @maria fyi for profiling.

sam: Run id run/2026-03-17/4512. Telemetry quick summary: batcher grouped more mixed-length batches, scheduler chose a fallback kernel for a subset of requests. Prefix cache (context cache) hit rate down ~18% for that run. Eval deltas: structured accuracy -5.2 pts, hallucination rate +3.8%. Small tail of JSON parse fails. Snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T22:12:01Z model=rwd-gpt-13b-quant-int4 kernel=fp8_compat fallback=true batch=32 lat=155ms -> 210ms
json-parser: error at token 42
```

maria: Profiler trace shows kernel_select() taking the fallback path when activation-scale for some tensors is outside the expected window. Also seeing extra host->device memcpy when prefix cache is missed. Flame excerpt: 
```
kernel_select.cpp:142 choose_kernel() -> fallback_path()
attention_kernel.cu launch 0x7f...
memcpy H2D 0x2a size=1.2MB
```
This explains both latency and the structured output misalignments (different kernel produces slightly different quant rounding).

alex: Is this tied to PR#4237 (the activation-scaling windowed update)? That changed per-tensor running stats and added clipping for extreme scales. If scale clips, quantized activations can underflow and we end up on the non-vectorized path.

kiran: Can we reproduce locally with a small script?

sam: Yes, repro command: 
```bash
python tools/repro_quant_regression.py --model rwd-gpt-13b --seed 42 --batch 32 --prefix-cache=false --scale-update=windowed
```
Running that toggles between stable and regressed behavior depending on whether windowed scale-update is enabled.

maria: I bisected to commit c3a9f4 — when I revert that commit, p95 returns to baseline and structured eval passes. The regression surface is flaky though: it only reproduces with mixed-length batches where batcher groups sequences with varied pad distribution, which triggers a different kernel selection path.

deploy-bot: rolling deploy for branch batcher-int4-scale completed at 2026-03-17T10:03:00Z.

alex: Proposed immediate actions: 1) revert PR#4237 from prod (sam), 2) add a unit/integration test that mixes variable-length batches and asserts kernel selection and output schema stability (maria), 3) add an eval regression alert for structured-output deltas > 2pts and p95 > 20% baseline (kiran), 4) investigate prefix cache invalidation when scale updates happen (maria+kiran). Also consider a short-term mitigation to force old kernel choice if cache/mixed-batch heuristic triggers fallback.

sam: Starting rollback now. If rollback shows improvement I'll keep prod pinned and open an incident ticket. Can we also hotfix to clamp scale to training stats to avoid triggering fallback?

maria: Draft hotfix idea: when activation scale deviates > threshold from training quantizer stats, clamp and emit telemetry counter. Pseudo: 
```c++
if (fabs(scale - trained_scale) > 0.5f) {
  scale = trained_scale;
  telemetry.inc("quant.scale_clamped");
}
```
This should avoid underflow-induced kernel switches while we root-cause the batching/scheduler interaction.

kiran: I'll queue the perf microbench and structured-eval suite against the rollback and the hotfix branch. Targets: run perf bench (batch sizes 1..64 mixed lengths), run structured eval with the hallucination probe set. I'll post results here.

alex: Owners: sam = rollback + prod monitor, maria = patch + tests, kiran = perf/regression runs + alerts. I'll file incident/INF-2026-014 and link the run ids.

sam: Rolling back now and will monitor traces/telemetry for kernel_select.fallback and quant.scale_clamped. Pinging #incidents if anything spikes.

maria: One more note — we should add a deterministic kernel-selection unit test (no GPUs) that exercises the quantization path and asserts identical output across scalar fallback and vectorized kernels within tolerance. That will catch future regressions before deploy.

kiran: Results queued, will report in ~30m. For now flagged prod -> degraded.

alex: Thank you all. Keep the thread updated with perf numbers and eval diffs. :thumbsup:
